analysis:
Reviewed the CHANGELOG.md head excerpts (lines 369-808), covering the v0.10.9 candidate notes plus retained v0.10.8 and v0.10.7 sections. The change is documentation only: no provider code, key handling, attestation path, or cache implementation is modified in the supplied evidence. I looked for places where the prose weakens the trust boundaries or contradicts the threat model, and found none.

The notes describe provider/cluster lifecycle behavior. Examples are cluster stop/start semantics, a stale pair part registering only as a pair member, a 15-minute idle stop, pair self-update drain/rollback, uninstall and revoke behavior, and disk-space checks. None of this alters the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), the App Attest authorization boundary (TB-011), or the prefix-cache posture (T-041). The notes keep the coordinator's reuse window at the already-signed-off 30 minutes and do not introduce new cache persistence.

Facts in the notes that depend on unseen code:
- Uninstall "revokes this Mac's account token where the coordinator can confirm it", which touches A-008 logout/revocation semantics.
- Pair self-update verification and rollback touch artifact integrity (T-013, T-043).
- The load-time page-cache clearing of model weight files is described as never changing file contents.
- The sandbox disk setup runs an installer and calls sudo diskutil enableOwnership only after a prompt, with no automatic format (TB-013, T-061).

I could not confirm any of these from the supplied changelog text alone. They are unverified contracts, not findings. The patch excerpt is truncated at the v0.10.9 rollout notes, and the v0.10.9 body beyond line 400 is not visible in the units supplied. The other-reviewer passes should check the code PRs behind these entries, in particular update/rollback verification, token revocation, and the add-on installer download integrity in TB-013.

No security regression is identified from this documentation-only evidence.
